items.question: The guardrail warrant curves for 2:1 embankments in the guardrail chapter assume what design speed?
items.note: No printed page number; RDM section label 3-1. Section 3-1, sentence under Figures 4 through 6: 'These curves are based on a design speed of 60 mph.'

items.question: Per Table 2 of the guardrail chapter, a shoulder drop-off steeper than 1:1 requires a traffic barrier when its height is greater than what?
items.note: No printed page number; RDM section label 3-1. Table 2 (T-2) Warrants for Nontraversable Hazards, row 'Shoulder drop-off with slope steeper than 1:1 (a) Height greater than 2 ft' = YES; (b) less than 2 ft = NO. Header 'Traffic barrier required' spans YES/NO.

items.question: In Detail 3-2A, what runout length LR applies at 60 mph with an ADT of 800 to 2,000?
items.note: No printed page number; RDM section label 3-2A. Detail 3-2A table (image only; page text layer holds just the header). Row 60 mph, column group 800-2000 ADT: LC 22, LR 330. Neighbours: 2000-4000 gives 360, under 800 gives 300.

items.question: What N width does Detail 3-2A give for a local or collector road with a design-year ADT of 400 to 1,500?
items.note: No printed page number; RDM section label 3-2A. Detail 3-2A, table 'N width for locals and collectors' under the merged 'Design year' header: under 400 = 2', 400-1500 = 5', 1501-2000 = 6', over 2000 = 8'.

items.question: Detail 3-2B: when L1 is equal to or greater than LC on the trailing end of a rigid obstacle, what anchor unit can be used because no L distance is needed?
items.note: No printed page number; RDM section label 3-2B. Note on Detail 3-2B (image): 'When L1 is equal to or greater than LC, no L distance is needed on trailing end of warrant. A CAT-1 anchor unit can be used.' Page 11 text says the same for multi-lane highways.

items.question: What recommended length of need L does Detail 3-2C give for a fill slope warrant at a 50 mph design speed?
items.note: No printed page number; RDM section label 3-2C. Detail 3-2C table (image only): 70 mph 150', 60 mph 125', 50 mph 100', 40 mph 75'.

items.question: For a hazard on a horizontal curve, how much is added to the tangent runout distance to get the total length of need?
items.note: No printed page number; RDM section label 3-2D. 3-2D: a distance of 12.5' is added to LH or LC.

items.question: What anchor deduction is used for a Type B-77 structure anchor unit when computing total guardrail length?
items.note: No printed page number; RDM section label 3-2F. Anchor Deductions table in 3-2F: GRAU-350 50.0', M-350 37.5', CAT-1 6.25', AT-1 6.25', *Type III 18.75', *B-77 22.875', *B-83 25.0'. Footnote: * measured from the end of the bridge or approach slab rail.

items.question: On a curb-and-gutter road faster than 35 mph, what berm width is needed to place guardrail at the preferred 12 feet from the face of curb?
items.note: No printed page number; RDM section label 3-5. 3-5: preferred placement 12 feet from face of curb; 'the berm width would have to be 14 feet'.

items.question: Median guardrail or guiderail is to be incorporated on freeway projects with medians of what width or less?
items.note: No printed page number; RDM section label 3-6. 3-6: 'median widths of 70 feet or less'. Page 21 says guardrail is not required in medians wider than 80' when the pier is centred (different rule, decoy).

items.question: Under a bridge, an outside pier at or closer than what distance from the edge of the main travel lane gets a concrete barrier plus guardrail?
items.note: No printed page number; RDM section label 3-7. 3-7 1.A: 'If the outside pier is 15'-6" or less from the edge of the main travel lane, use a concrete barrier and guardrail (Std. No. 857.01)'.

items.question: For a temporary bridge barrier with an offset of 4'-0" to 5'-11" from the edge of slab, which Roadway Standard Drawing barrier is used?
items.note: No printed page number; RDM section label 3-11. 3-11 (c): standard precast temporary concrete median barrier Std. No. 1170.01, restrained by the angle and anchor system; 0'-0" to 3'-11" uses the Type S barrier instead.

items.question: In Table 1 of the guardrail chapter (FHWA approved Type 350 units), how long is the SENTRE impact attenuator?
items.note: No printed page number; RDM section label 3-12. Table 1 (3-12) is an image on a rotated page; row SENTRE: width 2', length 17', supplier Energy Absorption, guardrail anchor unit (SF) and fixed object.

items.question: Who supplies the SKT 350 unit listed in Table 1 of the guardrail chapter?
items.note: No printed page number; RDM section label 3-12. Table 1 (3-12), row SKT 350: 1'-6" x 50', Road Systems, Inc. (FLEAT is also Road Systems; ET-2000 is Trinity).

items.question: Intersection bulbs are to be designed in accordance with which Policy and Procedure Manual section?
items.note: No printed page number; RDM section label 9-1. 9-1: 'Policy and Procedure Manual 23/1'; bulb-type intersections used on all divided facilities.

items.question: What minimum left or right turn lane length applies at a 50 mph design speed, and does it include the taper?
items.note: No printed page number; RDM section label 9-1. 9-1 F-4 table: 40 mph 330', 50 mph 550', 60 mph 680'; footnote '*This length includes the taper'. Taper-only values (230/265/300) are decoys.

items.question: What is the minimum taper length allowed within the minimum turn lane lengths of the right turn lane guidelines?
items.note: No printed page number; RDM section label 9-1. Footnote to the turn lane length table: 'The taper length can range from a minimum of 100' to a maximum of 150''. The maximum, 150', is the decoy.

items.question: In Table 3 (simple curve with taper), what offset is listed for a WB-100T design vehicle making a 45 degree turn?
items.note: No printed page number; RDM section label 9-2. Table 3 (T-3), angle 45, WB-100T: simple curve radius 200, radius with taper 115, offset 2.5, taper 15:1. The turn angle is printed only on the first row of each group.

items.question: What symmetric three-centered compound curve radii does Table 3A give for a WB-62 vehicle turning 45 degrees?
items.note: No printed page number; RDM section label 9-2. Table 3A (T-3A), 45 degrees, WB-62: symmetric radii 460-240-460 offset 2.0; asymmetric 120-140-500 offset 3.0-8.5.

items.question: Which AASHTO sight distance case gives the minimum required sight distance at a stop-controlled intersection?
items.note: No printed page number; RDM section label 9-3. 9-3: Case IIIA (vehicle crossing from the minor road) is the minimum required at unsignalized intersections; IIIB/IIIC are desirable.

items.question: What formula does Figure 3 of the intersection sight distance section use for the distance d along the major highway?
items.note: No printed page number; RDM section label 9-3. Figure 3 (F-3), legend: d = 1.47 V (J+ta); 12' lanes, level, right-angle intersections; based on 90 degree crossings and 0% grades.

items.question: What minimum length does the directional crossover drawing (9-4 Figure 1) require for all left turn lanes, including taper and storage?
items.note: No printed page number; RDM section label 9-4. Figure 1 of 9-4 (rotated sheet), note 6: 'Use 575' minimum length for all left turn lanes (includes taper and full storage length)'. Drawing assumes 46' median, 4' paved shoulders, 55 mph; 800' min. between crossover and U-turn.

items.question: What date is listed for revision 1.0 in the revision grid of the Signal System Timing Philosophy Manual?
items.note: Document Information page, D. Revision Grid: 1.0 12/25/2015 draft annotated outline; 2.0 2/1/2017.

items.question: What travel time reduction is the COST Section's performance goal for a retimed corridor?
items.note: Performance Goals, Table 1: new corridors 40%, retimed corridors 20% reduction in travel times.

items.question: What limitation does the data needs table list for traffic counts as a data source?
items.note: Data Needs and Applications table, row Traffic Counts, Disadvantages: 'Only 1 typical day of data (normally excludes Mondays, Fridays, rainy days & incidents). Only a snap shot in time'.

items.question: In Figure 1 (selection of objectives, strategies and tactics), which tactic is rated 3 for the Pedestrian Progression strategy?
items.note: Landscape matrix page with almost no text layer. Row 'Pedestrian Progression' has a single rating, a 3 under the tactic column 'Optimize Ped/Walk Time'.

items.question: What walking speed does the pedestrian progression strategy use?
items.note: Table 2 Strategies, Pedestrian Progression: 'walk at 3.5 feet per second'.

items.question: Below what volume-to-capacity ratio does the manual call a corridor undersaturated?
items.note: Degree of Saturation: undersaturated v/c less than 0.85; oversaturated v/c greater than 1.0.

items.question: In the cost benefit example, what is the peak hour total of the AM peak turning movement counts (Table 1)?
items.note: Cost Benefit Analysis Table 1: AM peak total 2522, noon 2408, PM 3381, sum 8311.

items.question: What cost per stop does the cost benefit analysis use?
items.note: Step 3 B: $0.014 per stop (AASHTO Manual on Road User Benefit Analysis); cost of delay $15.91/hour in 2015; 250 analysis days per year.

items.question: How far from the attraction can a TODS sign be placed at most?
items.note: Survey Procedures IV (printed page 3): G.S. 136-140.19(3), not more than five miles. The TOC on PDF page 2 lists 'Travel Services Inventory ... 3' and is a decoy.

items.question: To what precision is the odometer distance recorded on the TODS survey form?
items.note: Survey Procedures IV: 'Distance shall be recorded to the nearest 1/100 of a mile'.

items.question: If an attraction deleted from the TODS program for a breach re-applies and is found in compliance, what service charge per sign is paid to reinstall its signs?
items.note: VII.C (printed page 11): $160.00 per attraction sign. The $200 per sign charge for a design change (printed page 6) and the $200 contract fee are decoys.

items.question: Which TOD form is filled out when a TODS attraction changes ownership?
items.note: VII.D: Form TOD-5 'Change of Ownership', request within 30 days of actual transfer.

items.question: What retroreflective sheeting type is required on mini-TODS sign faces?
items.note: Appendix G item 3: mini-TODS Type I/engineering grade (enclosed lens); mainline TODS Type III/high intensity, the conflicting neighbour value.

items.question: According to the TODS application flow chart time frames, within how many days of the let date or contract execution should the signs be constructed?
items.note: Appendix flow chart (printed page 41), TIME FRAMES box: survey within 30 days of fee, fees within 60 days of approval, construction arranged within 7 days, signs constructed within 90 days; typical 6 months end to end.

items.question: How long do we have to keep fatal investigation files?
items.note: File Management: retained electronically according to standard policy (10 years).

items.question: What instrument do the field guidelines say to use to check curves at a fatal crash site?
items.note: Regional Office Field Guidelines item 4: 'Check curves with Ball Bank Indicator'.

items.question: What completion rate by the due date rates a Traffic Safety Unit engineer as 'Exceeds Expectations' on fatal investigations?
items.note: Performance Evaluation table: Exceeds > 95%, Meets 90-95%, Does Not Meet < 90%. The 60 calendar day expectation is a decoy.

items.question: In the functional-area reaction distance table of the access policy, what distance applies in an urban area at 45 mph?
items.note: Reaction Time and Distances table (printed page 27): Rural 2.5 s 130/165/200 ft; Urban 1.5 s 75/100/120 ft at 35/45/55 mph.

items.question: How much sight distance per 10 mph of arterial design speed does the access policy require for a single unit truck crossing a four-lane arterial?
items.note: Sight distance table (printed page 29): passenger vehicle 100/120/130, single unit truck 130/150/170, WB-50 170/200/210 for two/four/six lanes.

items.question: What is the maximum width of a one-way driveway under the NCDOT access policy?
items.note: Width of Driveways (W), printed page 50: one-way minimum 12 foot and maximum 24 foot; two-way maximum 36 foot. The 12 ft minimum and the 36 ft two-way maximum are decoys.

items.question: Which NCDOT district office covers Onslow and Pender counties?
items.note: Appendix 2 (printed page 68): Division 3 (Wilmington) - Jacksonville district office: Onslow, Pender.

items.question: Which General Statute requires abandonment of a road after 15 years of non-use, according to the Traffic Services Legal Guide?
items.note: Row 'Abandonment (non-use)': N.C. General Statute 136-96, last action 1987-0428.

items.question: Which Administrative Code rule holds the definitions for the Adopt-A-Highway Program?
items.note: Row 'Adopt-A-Highway Program (general) Definitions': 19A NCAC 2D.1002, last action 1993-1101. The column headers are printed only on page 1.

items.question: Under which Administrative Code rule does the Chief Engineer set maximum axle weights on light traffic roads?
items.note: Row 'Chief Engineer Powers (light traffic roads)': 4A.0106, last action 1993-1201.

items.question: What is the 'Last Action' session law listed for the church roads easement statute (G.S. 136-68) in the legal guide?
items.note: Row 'Church Roads (easements)': 136-68, last action 1995-0513; the table runs from page 1 with no repeated header.

items.question: On the DMV-349, what does the route class abbreviation PVA stand for?
items.note: Urban Non-Intersections section E listing: PVA = Public vehicular area; PP = private road, property or driveway.

items.question: For a rural non-intersection crash more than 500 feet from the reference point, the DMV-349 manual says 0.01 miles is about how many feet?
items.note: Rural Non-Intersections section H (table continues onto page 46): distance in feet if less than 500 feet, else nearest one-hundredth mile; '0.01 miles is about 53 feet'.

items.question: What vision obstruction code is entered on the DMV-349 when the driver was blinded by sunlight?
items.note: Driver Information table continues from page 52 (header 'Section / Enter' only there); L 34 Vision Obstruction: 9 blinded headlights, 10 blinded sunlight, 11 blinded other lights.

items.question: Per MUTCD Table 2C-1, what size is the Chevron Alignment (W1-8) sign on an expressway?
items.note: Table 2C-1 sheet 1 of 4 (printed page 148): W1-8 conventional 18 x 24, expressway 30 x 36, freeway 36 x 48, oversized 24 x 30.

items.question: What oversized dimension does MUTCD Table 2C-1 list for the Trail Crossing plaque (W11-15P)?
items.note: Table 2C-1 sheet 3 of 4 (printed page 150): W11-15P conventional 24 x 18, expressway 30 x 24, oversized 36 x 30. The header is repeated on each sheet but the sheet is a continuation.

items.question: Under MUTCD Table 2C-4 chart A, are horizontal alignment devices required, recommended or optional on an arterial without pavement markings carrying 1,000 to 2,999 AADT?
items.note: Table 2C-4 A (printed page 155): arterial/collector without markings: <1,000 optional, 1,000-2,999 recommended, 3,000-3,999 required, >3,999 required.

items.question: What chevron sign spacing does MUTCD Table 2C-5 give for a curve with a 35 to 45 mph advisory speed?
items.note: Table 2C-5 (printed page 158): 15 mph or less 40 ft, 20-30 80 ft, 35-45 (401-700 ft radius) 120 ft, 50-60 160 ft, >60 200 ft.

items.question: Per MUTCD 3B.02 guidance, center line markings should be placed on rural arterials and collectors at least 18 feet wide when ADT reaches what?
items.note: Section 3B.02 paragraph 02 (printed page 542): rural 18 ft and 3,000 vpd (guidance); urban 20 ft and 4,000 (guidance) or 6,000 (standard).

items.question: What minimum passing sight distance does MUTCD Table 3B-1 require for no-passing zone markings where the speed limit is 45 mph?
items.note: Table 3B-1 (printed page 543): 40 mph 600 ft, 45 mph 700 ft, 50 mph 800 ft.

items.question: In 23 CFR 655 Appendix Table 1 (daytime color limits for retroreflective material), what is the x chromaticity coordinate of corner point 1 for orange?
items.note: Table 1 to Appendix to Part 655 Subpart F (printed page 387): Orange point 1 x=0.558 y=0.352. y = 0.352 is the neighbouring cell.

items.question: What maximum daytime luminance factor does 23 CFR 655 Table 1A allow for yellow Type V retroreflective sheeting?
items.note: Table 1A (printed page 388): Yellow - Types I/II/III/VI min 15 max 45; Types IV/VII/VIII min 24 max 45; Type V min 12 max 30.

items.question: 23 CFR 655 Table 3A lists a fluorescence luminance factor YF of 15 for fluorescent red; may that value be used to judge performance in service?

accept: not as a measure of performance

items.note: Table 3A continued (printed page 389), footnote: YF values are typical, for quality assurance only; 'YF shall not be used as a measure of performance during service'.

items.question: What is the maximum daytime luminance factor for blue retroreflective pavement marking material in 23 CFR 655 Table 5A?
items.note: Table 5A (printed page 389): white min 35, yellow min 25, red 6-15, blue 5-14, purple 5-15.

items.question: Under 23 CFR 924.9, a Strategic Highway Safety Plan update must be completed no later than how many years after the previous approved version?
items.note: 924.9(a)(3)(i) (printed page 607).

items.question: What share of an incidental sidewalk project's cost does NCDOT pay for a municipality of 50,000 to 100,000 people?
items.note: The same population sliding-scale table appears on pages 4 and 11: >100,000 50/50; 50,000-100,000 DOT 60% local 40%; 10,000-50,000 70/30; <10,000 80/20. Either page is a correct citation.

items.question: Which countermeasure in the NCDOT interim design safety pilot project reduces vehicle turning speeds at intersections?
items.note: Printed page 13: curb extensions, median refuge islands, protected corners. The other two selected countermeasures (curb extensions, median refuge islands) are decoys.

items.question: How many candidate locations were on the pilot project team's initial list?
items.note: Printed page 15, last sentence: 'an initial list of 36 candidate locations'.

items.question: In the pilot project's initial candidate list, how many total crashes are recorded at Capital Blvd (US-1) and Calvary Dr in Raleigh?
items.note: Initial List of Candidate Locations (printed page 16): Capital Blvd (US-1) and Calvary Dr, Raleigh, Division 5, curb extensions, '5 pedestrian injury, 20 total crashes', shoulder.

items.question: Which highway division is listed for the Manning Dr and Ridge Rd/Skipper Bowles Dr candidate site in Chapel Hill?
items.note: Candidate list continuation (printed page 17): Chapel Hill, Division 7, intersection, curb extensions, 10 pedestrian injury, 11 total crashes.

items.question: What is the FHWA report number of the Guide for Improving Pedestrian Safety at Uncontrolled Crossing Locations?
items.note: Technical Report Documentation Page (printed page i): FHWA-SA-17-072, January 2018 (July 2018 updated), 38 pages.

items.question: Above what AADT does the STEP guide say a marked crosswalk alone is typically insufficient on a multi-lane road?
items.note: Printed page 16, citing Zegeer 2005: multi-lane crossings with AADTs exceeding 10,000. The underlying FHWA-HRT-04-100 Table 11 uses 12,000/15,000 thresholds, so the two documents differ.

items.question: In Table 1 of the marked-versus-unmarked crosswalk study, how many pedestrian crashes occurred at the marked crosswalk sites on 3- or 4-lane roads?
items.note: Table 1 (printed page 18): 3 or 4 lanes, marked 401 sites, 94 crashes; unmarked 395 sites, 12 crashes.

items.question: Per Table 7 of the crosswalk study, how many crashes were recorded at marked crosswalks on multilane roads without a raised median carrying 12,000 to 15,000 ADT?
items.note: Table 7 (printed page 23): Multi, no raised median, 12,000-15,000: marked 76 sites 23 crashes; unmarked 73 sites 2 crashes.

items.question: In Table 11 of FHWA-HRT-04-100, what recommendation code applies to a multilane road with a raised median, 12,000 to 15,000 ADT and a 35 mph speed limit?

accept: possible increase in pedestrian crash risk

items.note: Table 11 (rotated landscape page, printed 54): row 'Multilane (four or more lanes) with raised median', ADT >12,000-15,000 group, 35 mph column = P. Neighbours: 30 mph P, 40 mph N. The STEP guide's Table 1 is a near-duplicate matrix with different codes.

items.question: What minimum width must a raised median have to count as a pedestrian refuge in Table 11 of the crosswalk study?
items.note: Table 11 footnote ***: at least 1.2 m (4 ft) wide and 1.8 m (6 ft) long. The 6 ft (1.8 m) minimum length is the decoy.

items.question: In the split estimation example of the FHWA Signal Timing Manual (page 3-14), what average green time results for the EB through/right movement?
items.note: Critical movement table: EB TH/RT volume 485, 43%, split 52 s, Y+R 4 s, green 48 s. Footnote ** flags the NB LT 4 s green as possibly below minimum green.

items.question: What accident modification factor does the Signal Timing Manual cite for converting a 4-legged urban intersection from stop control to signal control?
items.note: Page 3-27: AMF 0.77 for all fatal and injury crashes, a 23 percent anticipated reduction.

items.question: Per Table 5-1 of the Signal Timing Manual, semi-actuated control is applicable where the major road is posted below what speed?
items.note: Table 5-1 (page 5-3), Semi-Actuated column: major road posted <40 mph, cross road light; fully actuated for isolated locations posted >40 mph.

items.question: In the HCM quick cycle-length estimate given in the Signal Timing Manual, what area type adjustment factor fa applies in a central business district?
items.note: Page 6-33: RS = 1,710 * PHF * fa, fa = 0.90 if CBD, 1.00 otherwise; minimum cycle 60 s.

items.question: What average maintained illuminance does Table 17 of the Signalized Intersections guide recommend for a Major/Collector intersection on asphalt (R2/R3) with a medium pedestrian classification?
items.note: Table 17 (printed page 92): R2/R3 block, Major/Collector: high 29.0 (2.9), medium 22.0 (2.2), low 15.0 (1.5). The R1 (concrete) block gives 15.0 (1.5) for medium, a decoy.

items.question: What ADT range defines a 'Collector' roadway for intersection illumination in Table 18 of the Signalized Intersections guide?
items.note: Table 18 (printed page 93): Major more than 3,500; Collector 1,500 to 3,500; Local 100 to 1,500.

items.question: Using Table 117 of the Signalized Intersections guide, Case II (exclusive left-turn lanes on the major approaches only), what planning-level capacity is given for three basic lanes on the major approach and two on the minor approach?
items.note: Table 117 (printed page 309), Case II: minor 1 lane 1,600/2,100/2,700; minor 2 lanes 2,100/2,600/3,000; minor 3 lanes 2,300/2,800/3,200 for 2/3/4 major lanes. Footnote ***: use a fraction of capacity for design.

items.question: What contract number is listed on the documentation page of the Pedestrian Facilities Users Guide (FHWA-RD-01-102)?
items.note: Scanned Technical Report Documentation Page: contract DTFH61-92-C-00138, 162 pages, Highway Safety Research Center.

items.question: How many different engineering improvements for pedestrians does Chapter 4 of the Pedestrian Facilities Users Guide detail?
items.note: Scanned abstract: 'Chapter 4 contains the details of 47 different engineering improvements'; 13 crash-type groupings in Chapter 3 is a decoy.

items.question: What maximum cross-slope does the Pedestrian Facilities Users Guide give for sidewalks?
items.note: Sidewalk Grade and Cross-Slopes (printed page 148): maximum cross-slope 1:50 (2 percent); curb ramp max grade 1:12 (8.3 percent); running grade 5 percent or less.

items.question: In Detail 3-2D (guardrail on the approach end of a hazard on a horizontal curve), what offset from the edge of lane is dimensioned at the GRAU-350 end, beyond N?
items.note: No printed page number; RDM detail label 3-2D. Image-only page drawn upside down; OCR reads 'GRAU-350', '0.75'', '+ N'. The drawing also dimensions 12'-6" along the curve (the 12.5' of 3-2D text on p14, a decoy).

items.question: In Figure 1 of the guardrail chapter (special grading in a superelevated location), what slope runs from the median shoulder break point down toward the ditch?
items.note: No printed page number; RDM label 3-6 F-1. Figure 1, image only; OCR reads '10:1' on all three sections (cross slopes .10, .03, .02 are decoys). Footnote: median shoulder width per Standards 560.01 and 560.02.

items.question: In the TODS manual's TOD-7 county list, what county code is assigned to Onslow County?
items.note: TOD-7 County List and Codes, second column group: Div. 3, Onslow, 067 (Northampton 066 and Orange 068 are neighbours). Printed page 21, PDF page 24.

items.question: What hourly rate does NCDOT pay contractors to mill shoulder rumble strips?
items.note: No pay rates anywhere in the tmsd documents.

items.question: How many fatal crash investigations did NCDOT complete statewide in 2019?
items.note: The Fatal Investigation Guidelines give procedures and deadlines, no counts.

items.question: What is the unit price per linear foot of GRAU-350 guardrail in the current NCDOT bid averages?
items.note: No prices in the guardrail chapter.

items.question: What in-vehicle sound level in decibels must shoulder rumble strips produce?
items.note: The rumble strip guidelines give geometry and placement only.

items.question: What runout length LR does Detail 3-2A give for an 80 mph design speed?
items.note: Detail 3-2A tabulates 40 to 70 mph only; the model must not extrapolate.

items.question: What was NCDOT's total HSIP apportionment for federal fiscal year 2024?
items.note: 23 CFR 924 sets program requirements, not dollar amounts.

items.question: What TODS fee does Virginia DOT charge for an attraction on a primary highway?
items.note: Other state; only the NC TODS manual is present.

items.question: What drop-off depth does the SCDOT require before temporary barrier is used in a work zone?
items.note: Other state and other division's topic.

items.question: What is the maximum deflection of NC-PCB portable concrete barrier on concrete pavement at 60 mph?
items.note: Answer lives in the wztc TMP Design Manual, not in any tmsd document; a refusal (optionally suggesting Work Zone Traffic Control) is expected.

items.question: What minimum cover does the Utilities Accommodation Manual require for a utility installed by bore and jack?
items.note: Utilities division document; must refuse for tmsd.

items.question: The 2004 rumble strip revision moved the strip from 6 inches out to 3 feet from the travel lane - when did that change take effect?
items.note: Reversed premise: the memo moved the strip from 3 feet to 6 inches (effective March 2005 letting). A correct reply refuses the premise or corrects it; it must not confirm the 3-foot placement. The rumble strip memo is not a registered tmsd document, so a refusal is the grounded reply; if it is registered later, a correction also passes.

items.question: Why does the guardrail chapter require a 500-foot minimum gap between separate guardrail installations?
items.note: The rule is the opposite: gaps of less than 300' should not be left; there is no 500-foot requirement.

items.question: What is the annual maintenance fee for a mainline TODS panel on an interstate exit ramp?
items.note: TODS are not installed on freeways or at ramp terminals; the $200 annual fee is per contract at non-freeway intersections. The premise is false.

items.question: The Signal Timing Philosophy Manual says undersaturated corridors have a v/c ratio below 0.95 - what ratio marks oversaturation?
items.note: The manual uses 0.85 for undersaturated and greater than 1.0 for oversaturated; the 0.95 premise is wrong and should be corrected or refused, not echoed.

items.question: According to the Fatal Investigation Guidelines, how many business days does a regional office have to review the DMV-349 before the 60-day clock starts?
items.note: No such pre-review period exists; the 60 calendar day (45 business day) expectation begins at Step 4 of the Tracker.
